Post-void residual PVR (ellipsoid formula) = coefficient k x width x height x depth, k about 0.52; less than 50mL normal, 50 to 100 mild, 100 to 200 moderate, not below 200 obvious urinary retention; emptying efficiency = voided volume ÷ (voided volume + PVR) x 100%.

Ask the patient to empty the bladder as completely as possible, then measure bladder width, height and anteroposterior diameter by transabdominal ultrasound and substitute them into the formula to estimate residual urine.
Ultrasound estimation carries some error; catheterization is needed for exact measurement. Residual urine >100 mL suggests impaired bladder emptying and warrants vigilance for BPH, neurogenic bladder and others.

map.一次测量异常要复查吗？: Should an abnormal single measurement be repeated?
map.要。残余尿受饮水量、排尿环境、紧张程度与测量时机影响很大，单次数值偏高很常见。临: Yes. Residual urine is strongly influenced by fluid intake, the voiding environment, anxiety and the timing of measurement, so a single high value is very common. Clinical practice usually requires a repeat on another day; only two consecutive values >100 mL are considered persistently significant, and medication or further testing is decided on that basis.
